title: Add GET /<short_code> redirect endpoint
approach: Add a new Flask route that captures a short_code path segment, looks up the corresponding Url record, aborts with 404 if not found, increments click_count, commits the change, and returns a 301 redirect to the original URL. Place the route after all explicit routes to avoid shadowing and import redirect and abort.
tests_to_write: test_redirect_success: create a short URL entry, issue GET /<short_code>, assert response status 301, Location header matches original URL, and click_count increased by 1.
test_redirect_not_found: issue GET /nonexistent_code, assert response status 404.
test_reserved_route_not_caught: ensure that requests to known static or health endpoints are not intercepted by the catch‑all route (status not 404 unless truly missing).
edge_cases: Short code does not exist → return 404.
Short code collides with reserved paths (e.g., static files, health checks) → treat as not found.
Database commit fails → roll back and return 500 (optional handling).
Concurrent requests may cause race condition on click_count increment (acceptable for simple app).
